NO. 018 · Songbirds & City Birds / Corvidae · Crows & Magpies

Large-billed Crow

大嘴乌鸦 · dà zuǐ wū yā Corvus macrorhynchos
Resident Common 46–52 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

The crow with the outsized bill

All black, with a bill so thick it looks exaggerated and a domed crown like a hat. The Large-billed Crow is surprisingly clever: it recognises faces, uses traffic to crack nuts, and organises the division of spoils at a refuse station.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • BillExtremely stout, the upper mandible clearly hooked at the tip and more than half the length of the head — the source of the name.
  • HeadForehead bulging and crown domed, clearly different from the flatter-headed carrion crow.
  • PlumageAll black with blue-purple or green-blue gloss; feather bases grey, visible if the plumage is parted.
  • TailWedge-shaped and medium in length, giving a rounded tail outline in flight.

Behaviour

Omnivorous and very intelligent, taking carrion, fruit, insects, eggs and human refuse, and caching food. Usually in pairs or family groups, strongly territorial. Resident here, from city high-rises to forest edges on the hills, concentrated around landfill sites and fishing harbours.

Voice

A deep, hoarse 'kaa-kaa-kaa', heavier and slower than the carrion crow's, with grunts and metallic whistles mixed in.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • city rooftops
  • around waste sites
  • Banzhang Hill
  • Jinwan seashore
Field note
Versus Black Kite: a crow flaps continuously and has a wedge-shaped tail; a kite soars and has a shallow fork. Flight action is the surest guide.
